title: The knight fork
summary: One knight, two targets. Learn to spot squares where a knight attacks the king and a valuable piece at once.

steps.title: How a knight attacks
steps.text: A knight in the middle of the board attacks eight squares, all of them in an L-shape. Its attacks cannot be blocked, and no other piece moves like it, so a knight can attack a queen or rook without being attacked back. A fork is a single move that attacks two pieces at once.
steps.narration: Watch the knight. From the middle of the board it attacks eight squares at once, all in that funny L shape, and nothing can block it. When a single knight move attacks two pieces at the same time, that's called a fork, and it's one of the strongest tricks in chess.

steps.title: Fork king and queen
steps.prompt: Win Black's queen with a knight fork.
steps.hint: Find the square from which the knight attacks both g8 and c8.
steps.success: Ne7+ checks the king and attacks the queen. Black must deal with the check, and the queen falls.
steps.narration: Time to hunt! Your knight on d5 can jump to a square where it checks the king on g8 and attacks the queen on c8 at the same time. Find that square, and the queen is yours.

steps.title: Fork king and rook
steps.prompt: The c7 square is undefended. Use it to win a rook.
steps.hint: From c7 a knight attacks e8 and a8.
steps.success: Nc7+ forks king and rook. You win a whole rook for nothing.
steps.narration: Here's my favorite fork of all. The square c7 is completely undefended: hop your knight there and it checks the king while attacking the rook in the corner. The king must move, and you take a whole rook for free!

steps.title: Why check helps
steps.question: Why is a fork that gives check especially strong?

options.text: The opponent must answer the check, so the other piece cannot be saved
options.why: Check takes away your opponent's choice. They have no time to move, defend or counterattack with the second piece.

options.text: A knight that gives check cannot be captured
options.why: A checking knight can be captured if something attacks it. The fork works because of what the check forces.
There are no points for checks. What matters is the material you win.

steps.narration: Last question. Why is a fork that also gives check so powerful? Think about what the check forces your opponent to do. Answer this, and you're officially a fork master. Great job today!
